clue.text: One involved in Asian cult movement in the Caribbean

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so the single letter goes within the other words
movement suggests the letters shift about and settle in a fresh order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has joined an Asian religious cult that is operating in the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the Caribbean' looks like the place where the cult is active, but it is the definition: SAINT LUCIA is an island nation there.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is loose: Saint Lucia is an island state located among the Windward Islands of the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: American state banks are to be reorganised

indicators.note: something reorganised is put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A financial news item: the banks in one US state face restructuring.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Great Plains of the Midwest.

clue.text: Stew for which soldier has a complaint

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner in it
gout is a painful ailment of the joints; 'has' just joins

explanation.surface: A soldier grumbles about the army stew he has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble about the food, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned French dish of meat and vegetables slowly cooked in sauce, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Final date in the Julian calendar?

definitions.text: Final date in the Julian calendar?

blocks.clueFragment: Final date in the Julian calendar?
blocks.note: surface reading: the last day of the year in the old Roman calendar Julius Caesar introduced
setter's reading: Julius Caesar's own diary, whose last entry was the day of his murder in March 44 BC

explanation.walkthrough: The Julian calendar is a real dating system, but 'Julian' here means belonging to Julius Caesar himself, who was assassinated on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides was the mid-month day, the 15th of March being the date Caesar was stabbed to death.

clue.text: Metal shackles keep men in step

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: brass bands are what keep marching men in step

blocks.note: brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
bands as bonds or fetters

explanation.surface: Iron fetters force a column of prisoners to march in step.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests chained convicts, but the music of a marching band is what keeps soldiers in step.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass bands play marches whose steady beat lets soldiers or parading men walk together in time.

clue.text: Oval jugs made by a foreigner

indicators.note: the letters are made, or fashioned, into something new, so they are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Egg-shaped pottery jugs crafted by an overseas potter.
explanation.walkthrough: JUGOSLAV is the older spelling of Yugoslav, a person from the former Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: To a British solver of the time, a Jugoslav was a native of Yugoslavia, hence someone from abroad.

clue.text: Here indeed is one man of genius

indicators.note: 'here' points at the words right in front of the solver, where the name sits in plain sight

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of indeed, all of is and the start of one

explanation.surface: A proud introduction: here, truly, is a genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb, is a byword for inventive brilliance.

clue.text: Did his influence make Rose change her name?

definitions.text: Did his influence make Rose change her name?

indicators.note: to change a name here is to alter the order of its letters into another word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Was it love that led a woman called Rose to marry and take a new surname?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: love's influence makes a bride change her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, whose influence would lead someone to wed and adopt a husband's surname.

clue.text: A channel swimmer accepts kiss from great man in history

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written
in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero
X is the cross for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A cross-Channel swimmer receives a kiss from a famous historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel; the swimmer is from myth and the channel is the Hellespont strait.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, king of Macedon, conquered an empire stretching to India and is among history's famous figures.

clue.text: Commanded by junior

blocks.note: first meaning: serving beneath someone's orders
second meaning: lower in rank or status

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a preposition for serving beneath an authority and as an adjective for lower rank.

clue.text: Contracts for polar missiles

blocks.note: N is the north, one of the two poles
arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Arms deals signed for missiles to be based in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' reads as business agreements, but it is a verb meaning gets smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow is to become less wide, so it contracts or shrinks in breadth.

clue.text: Work's returning, employs partners

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so these letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: OP is opus, a work, so work's gives the plural form
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone back at work again takes on business partners.
explanation.walkthrough: OP, short for opus, is a crossword staple for a work, especially a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a marriage partner, a husband or a wife.

clue.text: Famous composer? Hear, hear

indicators.note: the second 'hear' asks the solver to take the word by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: list is an old word for listen, as in 'list, list, O list' in Hamlet

explanation.surface: A cry of approval in parliament, as though applauding a celebrated musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear, hear' looks like a cheer of agreement; the first word is a synonym, the second the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer of the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: You may get a ride in it, if you're patient

definitions.text: You may get a ride in it, if you're patient

blocks.note: surface reading: a vehicle that gives you a lift if you are willing to wait
setter's reading: patient is a noun, a sick person needing hospital transport

explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective for willing to wait, but it is a person under medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: This emergency vehicle carries sick or injured people to hospital.

clue.text: It provides an opportunity for advanced theatrical work

definitions.text: It provides an opportunity for advanced theatrical work

blocks.note: surface reading: challenging, sophisticated drama for experienced performers
setter's reading: advanced means placed forward, a performing area jutting out in front of the curtain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' suggests a high level of skill, but it means physically projecting towards the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the part of a theatre's performing floor that extends forward beyond the proscenium arch into the auditorium.

clue.text: Choose to speak for the voters

blocks.note: to elect is to choose, often by vote
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Pick someone to be the spokesman for the people who vote.
explanation.definitionFit: An electorate is the whole body of people entitled to cast a ballot in an election.

clue.text: Source reference provided before the start of the lesson

blocks.clueFragment: Source reference provided before the start of the lesson
blocks.note: surface reading: a teacher citing a textbook before a class begins
setter's reading: the lesson is a Bible reading in church, announced with its exact location in scripture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lesson' suggests a school class; in church the reader first gives the book's section and line numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an exact citation, from the numbered divisions of the Bible, and so any precise authority.

clue.text: Worn thin perhaps, so it's included free

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given are only one possible arrangement of the result

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby secondhand item, so the seller throws it in at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown in is added as an extra without charge, a bonus with a purchase.

clue.text: Runners who jump the gun are not forgotten

definitions.text: Runners who jump the gun are

blocks.clueFragment: Runners who jump the gun are
blocks.note: first meaning: athletes who make a false start are called back to the line
second meaning: remembered, brought back to mind

explanation.walkthrough: To jump the gun is to start a race before the starting pistol fires.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both summoned back to the start after a false start and remembered.

clue.text: The followers stand here when assembled

indicators.note: assembled means put together from parts, so the letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a rally: supporters take their places at this spot once gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are supporters of a party, leader or faith, those who cling to its cause.

clue.text: Kind of robbery most likely to occur during rush hours

definitions.text: most likely to occur during rush hours

blocks.note: first meaning: a robbery at gunpoint

blocks.clueFragment: most likely to occur during rush hours
blocks.note: second meaning: a traffic delay, common when roads are busiest

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crime wave at peak time; the second half is the traffic jam sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an armed robbery and also a delay or stoppage, as in traffic jams.

clue.text: Understood one to be in diplomacy

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
tact is skill in handling people delicately

explanation.surface: Someone is tacitly expected to work in the diplomatic service.
explanation.definitionFit: A tacit agreement is implied or understood without being openly spoken.

clue.text: It doesn't describe the present schoolboy

definitions.text: It doesn't describe the present schoolboy

blocks.note: surface reading: today's pupils, the modern generation of schoolchildren
setter's reading: present means in attendance, so the boy described is absent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like it means modern-day, but it means in class, as at registration.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a child who stays away from school without permission, so is absent.

clue.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

definitions.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

blocks.note: surface reading: needing a like-minded companion to reach agreement
setter's reading: two people each with half a brain together make one whole mind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of one mind' is an idiom for agreeing; read literally, two half-minds add up to one.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or stupid person, jokingly said to have only half the usual intelligence.

clue.text: The boundary of laughter

blocks.note: first meaning: a sunken ditch that marks an estate's edge without blocking the view
second meaning: the sound of someone laughing

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a feature of English country estates: a hidden ditch serving as a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a landscaped trench marking a park's limit and the written sound of laughing.

clue.text: He has to exert some pull to make headway

definitions.text: He has to exert some pull to make headway

blocks.clueFragment: He has to exert some pull to make headway
blocks.note: surface reading: someone needing influence or connections to get ahead in a career
setter's reading: pull is the stroke of oars through water to move a boat forward

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' and 'headway' sound like office politics, but they describe rowing a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rower who propels a boat with a pair of oars, one in each hand.

clue.text: Swing - that's what killers did in olden days

definitions.text: what killers did in olden days

blocks.note: first meaning: to turn or slide round sharply

blocks.clueFragment: what killers did in olden days
blocks.note: second meaning: the old past tense of slay

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hanging, swinging from the gallows, as old punishment for killers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for veering round and the archaic past tense of slay, meaning killed.

clue.text: A nymph puts a spell on one

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
the Roman numeral for one, placed after; 'on' just joins

explanation.surface: A woodland sprite casts an enchantment over someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests magic, fitting the nymph, but it means a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a houri is one of the beautiful maidens of paradise, akin to a nymph.

clue.text: Container for spread

blocks.note: surface reading: a tub for butter or margarine
setter's reading: spread is urban sprawl, the growth of towns into countryside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like something for toast; it means the outward growth of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is a ring of protected open land around a town where building is restricted.
